item.title: More Acts Drop Off MAGA-Associated Rock The Country Festival
item.description: Earlier this month Ludacris was announced as a performer for the Rock The Country Tour, a country-centric traveling music festival with a MAGA slant. (Vocal Donald Trump supporters Kid Rock and Jason Aldean are headlining this year.) After facing backlash, Luda dropped off the tour, with his rep claiming that his inclusion on the lineup was "a mix-up." Now two more acts have removed their names from the lineup. item.title: Jeff Buckley Lands First Hot 100 Hit With 32-Year-Old Track
item.description: RIP Jeff Buckley, you would've hated TikTok, but at least you got a hit out of it. "Lover, You Should’ve Come Over," from the late singer-songwriter's only studio album Grace (1994), entered the Billboard Hot 100 this week at #97 after getting a major boost from TikTok. Not bad for a 32-year-old non-single! It's Buckley's first appearance on the Hot 100, coming nearly three decades after he tragically died of accidental drowning at age 30. item.title: Tate McRae & Justin Bieber Lead 2026 Juno Nominations
item.description: The Juno Awards, Canada's foremost music awards, have announced their 2026 nominees. For the second year in a row, Tate McRae leads the field. Her six nods tie her with Justin Bieber as this year's most nominated artist. As the CBC points out, the pop stars are nominated in the same six categories: TD Juno Fan Choice Award, Album Of The Year, Single Of The Year, Artist Of The Year, Songwriter Of The Year, and Pop Album Of The Year. item.title: Life Without Buildings Announce More Reunion Shows, First In 24 Years
item.description: Life Without Buildings have announced more reunion shows. Earlier this month the long-dormant Glasgow indie rockers announced a Nov. 20 show at London's KOKO to celebrate 50 years of Rough Trade. It's their first gig in 24 years, and it sold out in minutes. The band — whose only album is 2002's beloved Any Other City — added a second show Nov. 19 at the same venue, and that sold out too.
